title: Job Lifecycle, Resilience, and Operations
readerIntent: Configure, execute, restart, and recover jobs safely.
priorKnowledge: Know the job owner, schedule, handler, and side effects.
owner: CronJob definitions, scheduler, lifecycle services, and owning handler
summary: Create, update, run, start, stop, pause, resume, and remove operate on persisted definitions while runtime pools rebuild idempotently after restart.

sections.heading: Definition
items: Stable code, tenant, schedule, active state, handler, start/end, priority, node assignment, timeout, retry, overlap, idempotency, retention, and permissions.
Customer jobs belong in project modules; no arbitrary request service names, URLs, credentials, or executable handlers.

sections.heading: Resilience
items: Drain stops acquisition and process schedules while persisted definitions survive.
Restart rebuilds eligible schedules idempotently.
Node loss, network partition, and timeout can create uncertain outcomes; define duplicate policy, reconciliation, and compensation.
Retry only safe or explicitly idempotent work; process-local flags are not distributed locks.

sections.heading: Acquisition and overlap
paragraphs: Eligible nodes coordinate acquisition through the supported runtime contract. Process-local flags cannot prevent two different nodes from starting the same job.
The definition states whether overlapping runs are rejected, queued, coalesced, or permitted and how each run is identified.

sections.heading: Execution lifecycle
items: Resolve the persisted definition, tenant, node, handler, and authorization context.
Acquire within the overlap policy and create a run identity.
Invoke the owning handler with a deadline and scheduled service identity.
Record progress and safe diagnostics where supported.
Complete, retry, reconcile, compensate, or fail according to the contract.
Release acquisition and retain bounded history.

sections.heading: Misfire and time behavior
items: Declare time zone and daylight-saving behavior.
Define whether missed executions are skipped, coalesced, or replayed within a bound.
Prevent an extended outage from creating an unlimited replay storm.
Use a trusted clock and stable schedule parsing.
Test start/end and calendar boundaries.

sections.heading: Operations
items: Monitor scheduled, acquired, running, completed, failed, timed-out, retried, and skipped runs.
Alert on oldest pending age, duration, repeated failure, and node imbalance.
Pause acquisition before maintenance and drain bounded work.
Resume from persisted definitions and reconcile uncertain runs.
Archive history according to audit and privacy retention.

sections.heading: Evidence
items: Positive, invalid, unauthorized, cross-tenant, schedule boundary, manual run, overlap, timeout, retry, restart, drain, node loss/return, recovery, reconciliation, performance, integration, and regression tests.

sections.heading: Security
paragraphs: Create, update, manual run, pause, resume, and removal are authorized operations. Handler and parameters come from governed definitions, not arbitrary request values.
Scheduled service identity remains separate from human login and receives only target permissions required by the handler.
